pages.lesson:
LESSON: POPULATION DISTRIBUTION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Population
Topic 2.2: Population Distribution

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Population Distribution. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How is population spread out in the county?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe patterns of population distribution in the county

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. describe patterns of population distribution in the county
   In simple words: practise until you can describe patterns of population distribution in the county. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Population Distribution using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Population Distribution in the examples.
2. Explain Population Distribution to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Population Distribution.
4. Show that you can: describe patterns of population distribution in the county

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Population Distribution using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Population Distribution important for a Grade 4 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Draw a map of the county showing population distribution,
2. Digital Literacy: Learners use a digital or print map of the county to identify the patterns of population distribution.
3. Learning to Learn: Learners develop relationships as they share diagrams of the patterns of population distribution in class. Values:
4. Responsibility: Learners develop self-drive as they share the diagrams of the patterns of population distribution in class.
5. Integrity: Learners have self-discipline as they use a digital or print map of the county to identify the patterns of population distribution. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs):

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. describe patterns of population distribution in the county

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
